adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.css.scss:89 - introducing dark-light-choose in standalone embed stylesheet may not resolve scheme/variables correctly for third-party pages, rendering embedded comments with the wrong hard-coded branch

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce `dark-light-choose(...)` into the standalone `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` (`a.new-user` color), whereas previously it used a single `scale-color($primary, ...)`. That makes the embed stylesheet’s output potentially depend on the availability/behavior of `dark-light-choose` (and any assumptions it makes about light/dark scheme selection), which could be a concern for embeds rendered on third-party pages. However, the diff alone doesn’t show how `dark-light-choose` is implemented or whether embeds include the necessary scheme selectors/variables, so this is a plausible scope/compatibility concern rather than a verifiable defect from the patch itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/topic-post.scss:291 light-theme branch value silently changed from 30% to 70% lightness, making quote-link text washed out for light-theme users

This likely makes the link much lighter in light theme and appears unintended.

Assuming `dark-light-choose(light, dark)` (as used consistently elsewhere in the diff), the light-theme branch has indeed drifted from 20% to 50%, which is a concrete, diff-verifiable visual change/regression in the light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: mobile/modal.scss:99 .custom-message-length light branch flipped to 30% lightness (near-black instead of faded), moving in the wrong direction relative to sibling rules in desktop/modal.scss

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss` at `.custom-message-length`, the change replaces `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` with `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`. This makes the light-theme (first argument) branch much darker (30% lightness) instead of the prior faded/light 70%, and it is inconsistent with the corresponding rule in `desktop/modal.scss` which uses `dark-light-choose(...$primary 70%..., ...$secondary 30%...)`. The diff therefore verifiably introduces an inverted light/dark choice for this specific mobile rule.

adjudication_records.issue_text: desktop/user.scss:519 and mobile/user.scss:494 .name color changed such that .name and .title on the user card become identical, destroying visual hierarchy

The same pattern occurs in mobile/user.scss. This makes `.name` and `.title` use identical colors, which is a verifiable visual regression (loss of intended contrast/hierarchy) introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.css.scss:89 uses dark-light-choose() which may not be in scope for the embed compilation context, risking a build break or wrong value for one of the two embed palettes

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show embed.css.scss now calling `dark-light-choose(...)` (e.g., `a.new-user { color: dark-light-choose(...) }`). The finding raises a build/compilation-scope concern specific to this newly introduced usage in the embed stylesheet. However, the diff alone does not show whether `dark-light-choose` is or isn’t available in the embed compilation context, so the risk cannot be verified from this PR content.

adjudication_records.issue_text: ~70 hand-expanded copies of the dark-light-choose complement pattern should be replaced with a single SCSS mixin to eliminate drift-prone duplication

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces many occurrences of `scale-color($primary, $lightness: ...)` with explicit `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary,...), scale-color($secondary,...))` across numerous SCSS files. This creates substantial duplicated, hand-expanded logic (dozens of near-identical expressions) that is drift-prone if the complement mapping needs to change later. A mixin/function would centralize the pattern and reduce maintenance risk. This is a maintainability/architecture concern introduced by the change, not a runtime defect.
